chunks: It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ghurāb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Do not testify to a testimony until you know it as clearly as you know your own palm.

key_terms.تَشْهَدَنَّ: to bear witness or give testimony emphatically
key_terms.تَعْرِفَهَا: to know it with certainty and clear recognition
key_terms.رُوِيَ: it is narrated, indicating transmission of the report
key_terms.شَهَادَةٍ: testimony given in a matter requiring witness
key_terms.كَفَّكَ: your palm, used here as a comparison for direct and unmistakable knowledge

ai.seo_question: When is a person allowed to give testimony in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs that testimony must only be given on the basis of clear and certain knowledge. It emphasizes caution, accuracy, and personal certainty in matters of witness-bearing, which is essential for justice and the protection of people's rights.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3359 - It is narrated from Ali ibn Ghurab, from Abu Abdillah (as):
Imam (as) said: "
Do not testify to a testimony until you know it as clearly as you know your own palm."
